■‘Whether the action of the management of Reserve 
Bank of hidia, Bombay in relation to their New 
Central Office Building, Bombay in taking the work 
of filing papers from Telephone Operatons is justi¬ 
fied 7 If not, to what relief are the workmen con¬ 
cerned entitled 7” 

2. ll seems that the Reserve Bank of India has got two 
office buildings in the Fort area that is the old building 
known as Main Office Building and the other what is known 
as New Central Office Building, which was commissioned 
sometime in November, 1980. The present dispute relates 
to the Telephone Operators .serving In the New Central 
Office Building. Now the contention of the Upion which is 
espousing the cause of those Telephone Operators is that the 
inanapmcnt has no right to assign clerical duties to these 
Tclcpnane Operators which they have siartcd doing from 
the year 1970 onwards by includ ng suitable condition in the 
.appointment order which condition was non-jxistent in the 
past. On this way it is urged that these Telephone Operators 
who belong to non-clerical .staff are being required to per¬ 
form clerical duties but at the same time they arc denied 
promotional avenues which are available to the members of 
clerical staff In this way it is complained that there is two 
fold d s-advantage in the first instance additional duties are 
expected from these Telephone Operators and secondly no 
promotional avenues arc made avail.nble, the Telephone 
Operators being required to remain in the same cadre and 
capacity till the time of Iheir retirement. It is urged that in 
this manner there is a change in the condition of service 
effected by the management that too without following the 
procedure laid down under Section 9A of the Industrial Dis¬ 
putes Act and therefore the same is bad and illegal and 
therefore requires to be struck down. 

3. The contention is opposed on two grounds firstly that 
the individual dispute has never achieved the character of 
an industrial dispute, the Union who is espousing the came 
having no substantial backing and not n recognised union. 
Secondly it is urged that what duties are to be_ assigned to 
the Telephone Operators is a part of Managerial Function 
and therefore if certain additional duties are allotted hv 
virtue of Reserve Bank of India (Staff) Regulation, 1948 
these workmen are expected to carry out those duties with¬ 
out any murmur and smee the item did not form part of 
the Fourth Schedule Reel ion 9 A can never be attracted and 
as such no grievance can be raised against the said ass'.gn- 
nicnt of duties.

8 . It was urged on behalf ,if the Ijanl: hy Shi i Nijampnr-

about a change and may curtail or augment the po-ryevs 
to be exercised certain authorities. Here the first change 
was effected by the Award what is known as Saslri Award 
and then again there was a confirmation of the said change 
by Bipartite Settlement of the year 1966. Conseonently if 
the parties by their own action have restricted the powers 
of the authorities and laid down certain specific procedure, 
it is not the General Law but the law as contemplated by 
the parties which would govern the right of the cmploycr.s 
and the employees, We therefore cannot fall back on 
General Law to hold that the Appointing .Authority is also 
by virtue of his po.st becomes the Disciplinary Authority 
empowered to take suitable disciplinary action like the

The Central Government in exercise of its power,s confer¬ 
red under Section 10 Of the Industri.al Disputes Act, 1947, 
referred the following matter for adjudication 'idc NoiiJiea- 
fion No, L-400I2(9)83-D,II(Bj dated 13th June, 1984:-- 

“■Whether the action of the management of General 
Manager {Telecommunications) Bhopal in terminat¬ 
ing the services of S/Shri Sunil Sen, Abdul Rafiq, 
Abdul N,alm. Shaniaram Radke. Ntithoo Atkar. Ram 
Sahay Sharma. M.S. Pandev. B, 'Vinod w.e.f. .31-5-83 
without payment of retrenchment compensation etc. 
and instead employing new person.s sponsored by 
the local Emnlovraent Exchange is justified ? If not. 
to what relief the workmen concerned arc entitled ?” 

2, The facts in this c-isc lie in a very brief rompas,s. Eight 
workmen were all casual employees of the Telecommunica¬ 
tions. P^rT Department, For a regular reerriitment in the 
Postal services a.s labour they have to he spon.sored by the 
Employment Exchance. How'ever, these workmen being casual 
workers were employed by ihc Po.stnl Dcpartmcnl ihough 
they had not been .sponsored by the Employment Exchange. 
It is undisptilcd that all the eight workmen hate completed 
more than 240 davs hbforc ihn Iasi date they were ..mplovcd 
by the Post and Telc.eraph Dcpailment. ‘lOine of them have 
worked for re.ni'ly four ctiij's, Prnclic.nllv everyone li.'id been 



1305 


vrKar WTTim: irr# 9, i 985 [m^ i s, isoe 


[»rrtr 3(ii)] 


employed by ihe Postal Department for about two years. 
As stated by the workinen and as would be clear Iroin 
the order of reference they were not given employment afier 
31-5-1983 and instead some other persons were employed in 
their place. The question, therefore, lhat arises is whether 
the department was justijied ir, doing .so, the above workmen 
Waving completed 240 days Vv'ilhin a period of 12 months 
before -31-5-1983. The answer is not difficult to seek. Since 
the postal department is an industry it is governed by the 
provisions of the Industrial Disputes Act. Section 25F lays 
down that no workman employed in any. industry who Jias 
been in continuous service for not less than one year under 
an employer shall be retrenched by the employer until cer¬ 
tain conditions provided in the section have been fulfilled. 
S.ection 25B of the Act provides that for the purpose of this 
Chapter and for the purposes of the Se-tion a workman 
si’all be said to be in continuous service for a period of 12 
months if he is in the uninierrupted service including service 
which may be interrupted oh account of sickness or autho¬ 
rised leave or an accident or a strike which is not illegal 
or a lockout or cessation of work which was not due to 
any fault on the part of the workmen, 'the workmen con¬ 
cerned here being casual labourers were only called for 
work when necessary. Naturally, they would not come within 
the definition of continuous service as provided in Sub¬ 
section (1) of Section 25B. However, Section 25B(ii) lays 
down that where a -workman is not in continuous servi e 
within the meaning of Clause (il for a period of one year 
or six months he ^shall be deemed to be in continuous service 
under an employer— 

(a) for a period of one year, if the workman during 
a period ot twelve calendai' months preceding the 
date with refersnee to which calculation is to be 
made, has actuilly woiked under the employer 
for not less than— 

(i) one .hundred and ninety days in the case of a 
workman employed below giound in a mine; and 

(iif two hundred and forty days in any other case. 

The workmen concerned hers have worked for more than 
240 days. Therefore they will be deemed to be in continuous 
service for more than a year.' That being so. Section 25F 
is clearly attracted. Since the mandatory provisions as pro¬ 
vided in Section 25F were not observed their termination 
from services is void. The effect of tlie continuous service 
rendered by the workmen concerned would be that they 
were entitled to be continued in the work and if the mauage- 
ment wanted to dispense with their services they have to 
be retrenched according to ihe provisions ot the Iridasirial 
Disputes Act and particularly Section 25F, Sectio,T 25G and 
25H. I would, therefore, direct that the above workmen are 
entitled to be continued in work. 

3. The question then would arise about their back wages. 
The workmen have stated before me lhat if they are regu¬ 
larised they would not make anv claim for back wages. The 
management here point-ed out that the instructions are that 
they should not recruit any one who had not been sponsored 
through the Employment Exchange. It would be seen that 
the instructions given to them cannot over ride the provisions 
of the Indusrtial Disputes Act. I would direct that the above 
applicants be absorbed in the department according to their 
seniority as and when vacancies arise. They are certainly 
entitled to be employed in preference to those casual labour¬ 
ers who have been recruited subsequently. As regaids back 
wages. I direct that if the department absorbs the above 
eight applicants within a period of two months thev w'ill not 
get any back wages. Hovvpver. if such order is rot made 
within two months from today the appli 'an^s would eel half 
the back wages and would be entitled to r.e-em.ployed as slated 
earlier. There shall, however, be no order as to costs in 
the peculiar circumstances of the case,

'ndu-strial estabh'sbm.ent in Coal Mines defines a “Padli”

sti-n'iinr. Orders defines a badli workrnan, A “Badli” or 
siihrti'titp is one 'vho is appointed in the PO*-t of a permanent

vacated by th® permanent workman or probationer. It further, 
states that a “Badli” working in place of Probationer would 
be deemed to be a permanent after co^itpletjon of the 
probationcry period. Under Clause 3(b) a permanent work¬ 
man is donned. A permanent workman is one who is ap¬ 
pointed for an unlimited period or who has satisfactorily 
put in 3 months continuous service in a .permanent post as 
Probationer. From the evidence discussed above it will ap¬

os such the concerned workman cannot he said to be a

himself a permanent workman. In the above view of the, 
matter r hold that the concerned workman wa<i only a badli 
workman working as Night Guard during the sick vacancy 
of Chandra Bahadur. A person working in a temporary 
vacancy caused bv the absence, of a permanent workman can¬ 
not be said to he a permanent workman as actually no 
permanent vacancy is c.aused in as much as the workman 
who has gone on leave is actually on the permanent post. 

In view of the fact that the concerned workman was 
only, a badli casual worker working as Night Guard, there 
Was no need to give notice to him under Section 9A of

ed on the date Sh. Chandra Bahadur join^ as Night Guard 
and automatically there was no post of Night Guard to em¬ 
ploy the concerned workman. 

Taking the entire facts, evidence and circumstances of the 
case into consideration, I hold that the demand of Rashtriya 
Colliery Mazdoor Sangh for rcstoiation of Shri Kali Charan

that the conccnicd workman is not entled to any relief.

AWARD 

Ihe Government of India in the Ministry of Labour and 
Rthahilitation in exercise of the powers confeiied on them 
under Section 10|l;(d) of the I.D. Act, 1947. has rcfcired 
the following dispute to ffiis Tribunal lor adjudication under 
Order No. .D2(X>12(12(yyS3-D.m(A) dated the iyih/20th 
December, 1983. 

SCHEDULE 

“Whether the action of the management of' Messrs. 
Bharat Coking Coal Limited, Dhanbad in disconti¬ 
nuing increments after 12 months from the pay of 
S/Shri Chanchal Kumar Bancrjce, S. K, CnaKxa- 
borty, P. K. Chakraborty. Rohit Kumar Chawrk and 
, M, A. Raja, ganted in terms of their Office Ogifcr 

No. l/67/1067(Hj dated 17th January, 1977, when 
in other cases such special increments granted have 
been merged in the pay, is justified and reasonable? 

If not, to what relief are the said workmen en¬ 
titled 7” 

The base of the workmen is that the management of BCCL 
issued a circular dated 17-1-77 for cncoura.ging the use 01 
Hindi in the working of the management. The said circulai 
provided incentives to the employees. It was provided as in¬ 
centive to the employees that non-Hindi speaking employees 
pas.sing Hindi typing test held by the management would be 
given two increments as incentives. The management of BCCL 
were conducting typing and shorthand test in Hindi anc. 
special increments were awarded to the employees in accor¬ 
dance with the above drcnlar from 1977 to 1979 and ibt 



1312 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA;MARCH 9. 


increinents granted to them was liormiincnt in niitiire and it 
was never withddawn. T]^ manaeoment of BCGL conducted 
Hindi shorthand and typing test on 3-6-80 under the provi- 
. 1.1 of the above oiroilar in which the conccm'jd workman 
appeared in the tcsi and were declared sucoejsful by the 
management. The manasement by an Office Order dated 
17-6-81 issued an order grunting two special increments to 
the concerned workmen for 12 months only. Jt is submitted 
on behalf of the workmen that the above order was violating 
the provisions of the circular dated 17-1-77 as no modifi¬ 
cation and supersession was made in the *aid circular. Thlre 
was no justification for the management for granting incre¬ 
ments to the concerned workmen for 12 months only and 
they should have got the increments permanently as other Work¬ 
men who had passed the examination previously were getting. 
The management has discriminated b’v way of granting incre¬ 
ments of 12 months only to the concerned workmen. The 
workmen passing Hindi typing and short hand test previously 
are still cnioving the benefit of circular. The workmen re¬ 
presented before the authorities fior removal of the discri¬ 
mination but their grievances were r/>t considered. Thereafter 
they approached the union and the union took up their case. 
When the union failed to settle the dispute under code of 
discipline and ioint discussion, an industral dispute was raised 
befori^ the ALCIC). The conciliation before Ihe ALCfCl failed 
and thereafter the Government of India referred this dispute 
for adjudication. 

The case of the management is that the reference is not 
maintainable. The Head OfBpc of M/s. B'.C.C. Ltd. where 
the concerned workmen wef^ working is not a mine and as 
such the reference is bad. Tho management in order to 
popularise Office wok in Hindi gave an incentive to learn 
Hindi typing/Hindi sborthar.d and the management on its own 
discretion decided to grant sesme advance increments for a 
limited period to suoh employees who passed Hindi short¬ 
hand/Hindi type writing and issued an Office Order dated 
17.-1-77. The said offloe crd«h is not a settlement within the 
meaning of Clause fP) of Section 2 of the ID. Act. the 
said circular was purely voluntary and discretionary and its 
non-implementation cannot form the subject matter of in- 
dustriffi dispute as the same is not binding either on the 
employers or on the v/oritmen. The grant of advance incre¬ 
ments as mentioned in the circular was con¬ 

fined only to one or two advance increments but 
it was not meant to be allowed throughout the 
tenure of employment of the employees concerned on perma¬ 
nent basis. Any demand for conlinuation of the said advanoc 
Increment on permanent ba.sl.s is not justified and reasonable. 
Due to wrong interpretation bv some officers of the manage¬ 
ment some emnlovees were allowed to rorit'niie the advance 
increments bevond two years for which ne''esaary leva! ac¬ 
tion is taken for meovery. 0| the above niea *t was s''b- 
mitted that the action of the manacomeUt for dlsrontinning 
inerempTitc atifr 12 months to the concerned workmen was 

fpilv Instifled , 

The simple question to be decided in this case is whether 
the discontinuing of the increments after 12 months to the 
oopoerned -workmen was justified. 

The management have examined one witness and the work¬ 
men examined two witnesses in support of their cases. Besides 
that the workmen have exhibited seven documents and the 
management have exhibited 12 documents. 

In nutshell the entire case hinges on the interpretation of 
Ext. ljV-1 which is the Office order dated 17-1-77. The manage- 
nyfjit has al^o exhibited the said circular dated 17-1-77 which 
is marked Ext. M-12. Ext. W-l and M-12 are the same. The 
said circular dated 17-1-77 shows that the management had 
issued the said circular in order to spread the use of Hindi 
in the office for which incentives were given to the employees 
working -with the management, We arc here concerned with 
the non-Hindi speaking employees who have passed the Hindi 
typing c.'tamination held by the management and the in¬ 
centive for the same is provided in para 2(a) of the said 
circular. It provides that non Hindi speaking employees 
passing Hindi typing test -will get two increments m their pay 
as special pay. 'There is no rime limit provided in the said 
circular and it appears that this incentive in the increment 
of the pay was not for a limited period of 12 months or of 
any other specified period. On further analysis of this circniar 
it will give an impression that the increments granted was 
permihent in nature. This appears to h© dear if we refer to 


1985/PHALGUNA 18, 1906 [Part 11— Sec. 3 (ii)] 


danse 2(b) of the said circular where it is provided that Hindi 
speaking employees passing short hand test -will be promoted 
to the higher grade. This promotion to a higher grade cannot 
be limited for a limited period nor there is any such limit 
regarding the period of the said promotion of the 
employee. If this promotion in the higher grade was to be 
given permanently, it is clear that the increments which was 
to be given under Clause 2(a) to the non-Hindi speaking em¬ 
ployees was of a permanent nature. In my opinion tne circular 
gave the increments pcrmanoutly as special pay to the em¬ 
ployees who passed the said test. 

Ext. W-2 dated 30-1-79 Is an Office order by which incre¬ 
ments were given to the employees who had passed tlie test 
In Hindi typing and Hindi shonhand. The said Office order 
has not limited the period of increments which was given to 
the 33 'employees who had passed the said test. Ext. W-3 is 
the Office order dated 7-2-81 which shows that two.persons 
passed the test and that one Tarun Kumar Mitra was given 
two increments in his salary but no limit of this increment 
was stated In the office order. Ext. W-5 dated 5-5-81 is the 
Office order which shows that the concerned five workmen 
who were non Hindi speaking employees had passed Hindi 
typing examination but it was ordered that they would get 
the increinents only for 12 months on furnishing certificates 
that they are non-Hindi speaking, Ext. W-6 dated 17-6-81 Is 
the Office order which shows that the concerned workmen 
furnished their certificates that ffiey were non-Hindi speaking 
employees and that they were to get two increments for 12 
months only. The management has not produced any circular 
to show that the circular dated 17-1-77 was modified. Ext. W-7 
is a letter dated 17-1-84 which shows that the circular da’ed 
17-1-77 has not been superceded by any Office order. T5o 
management has not filed any office order to show that there 
has been any modification or suspercession In the circular dated 
17-1-77. hfW-l has stated that there is no mention in Ext M-12 
that incentive was to be paid onlv for 12 mouths. It ’-vtil uNo 
appear from his evidence and the circular Ext. M-12 iUdf 
that this circular was passed by the Board of Directors ',f 
the management. MW-1 has stated that the General Manager 
cannot supercede the order of the Directors. Thus the order 
passed in Ext. \V-5 by Upkarmik Prahandhak is not in ac¬ 
cordance with the circular Ext. M-12, He was not authorised 
to make any modification in the circular which was passed 
by the Managing Director of the Company. On this account 
also the order in Ext, W-5 for payment of two increments 
only for 12 months cannot be sustained. 

Ext. W-4 dated 21-3-80 shows that in accordance W'lth the 
circular dated 17-1-77 employees passing the Hindi shorthand 
and Hindi typing examination were given increment but there 
was some confusion in fixing the salary of those employees 
after the irnffitmentation of NCWA-II Hence it provided that 
at the time of fixing the pay of such employees who have 
passed silch examination the new scale should be fixed on 
the basis of their pay as on December, 1978 without including 
the increments which were aUowed on ground of p.assing the 
test and after the fixation in new pay scale tw'o further incre¬ 
ments be paid to them in the new pay scales. It appears there¬ 
fore that the Inorements granted were permanent because here 
also there is no mention of the fact that such increments 
granted were to be granted only for a limited period of 12 
months. 

In view of the discussion made above I hold that the two 
increments which were granted to the concerned workmen 
wire of a permanent nature and that the increments could 
not be limited for a period of 12 months only. 

It has been submitted on behalf of the management that 
the concerned workmen aie not working in the Mines and 
as such the reference is bad. It will appear that the concerned 
workmen are working in Materials Management division which 
is a section of the Headquarters Office under the control and 
administration of M/s, B.C.C. Ltd. The said materials manage¬ 
ment division deals with purchase of materials required for 
use in the production of coal and as such the concerned 
workmen are engaged in the work which is incidental or con- 
necction with mining operations. The coal is mind with the 
materials which are purchased and are supplied in the pro¬ 
duction of coal and the concerned workmen are employed for 
the said purpose and as such in my opinion their work is 
connected with mining operations and the Tribunal has juris¬ 
diction to adjudicate this case.

In view of the above discussion I hold that the action of 
the management of B.C.C. Ltd. in discontiniiiiig increments 
after 12 months from the pa.v of the concerned Workman 
granted in terms of the circular dated 17-1-77 is not justilied 
and reasonable. The concerned workmen are entitled to the 
said increment pMmanently from the date of the said incre¬ 
ment has been discontiiuicd and the management is directed 
to pay the same to the concerned workman. 

This is my Award.

tion 15(4) states that nn employee who was satisfactorily 
completed his probation in arty post shall thereafter be con¬ 
firmed. Admittedly, the workman Shri Badole worked in the 
promoted post of a Dusting Operator for more than three 
years i.e. from 20-1-1971 to 1(3-2-1974. Witness No. 1 Shri 
y. Ramkrishna Sharma, examined by the Corporation, stated 
in his cross-examination ;— 

“T do not know if tliere is any provision under which 
a confirmed employee can be reverted on his trans¬ 
fer on his own request. It is true that as per order 
dated 8-3-1983 (pnn.-R) Shri K. R. Bopte, Dusting 
Operator w'as transferred from Jabalpur to Nagpur 
and he continued to work as Dusting Operator and 
was not reverted as Watchman." 

Thus, this witness could not .show any provision under 
which a confirmed employee can be reverted on his liansfer 
on his own request. On the other hand, in ills examination- 
in-chief as well as in .his o o.s.s-examination, he admitted that 
when an employee is transferred nf his rennest, he becomes 
the juniormost in the cadre at the place or his transfer. Thus, 
according to him. Shri Badole became iunior-most in the 
cadre of Dusting Operator when he was transferred to Nag¬ 
pur from Madhya Pradesh in 1972. In the face of this volu¬ 
minous documentary evidence r>n record and in the face of 
the arfmis^ione given by the same witness, ft is clear that 
workman Shri Badole was not wlHing to accept the reversion 
a,s Watchman and hence, he was issued transfer orders dated 
14-3-1974 and 21-3-1974 and he wa.s forced or cnerced to 
give a writing fannexnre-E dated .5-4-1974 showing his wilUnB- 
ness for reversion to the I30st of Watchman. Thus, the action

inlndictons and against the provisions of Staff Reaulntlons.

higher in grade than that of a Watchman and normal pay of 
Dusting Operator is higher than that of a Watchman. Not

*he terms of the scttlmcnct and as such he was reinstated. 

It will appear from the W.S. of the maniigcmcnt that a 
t.awycrs notice was given,on behalf of Piyasi Dcvi widow 
of Jitu Dhoba before me management alleging that the 
concerned workman had fradulcnily got reinstatcrayit in 
nlucc oi' Jitu Dhoba, Erom the Eorm U Register Ext. M-I9 
H, will appear that there was no workmen named Jitu Dhoba 
in it. In the Award and the settlement Ext, M-8 and M-12 
also there was no mention of the name of Jitu Dhoba. Thus 
there does not appear to be any evidence that the concerned 
workman had got reinstatement by falsely representing him¬ 
self as Jitu Dhoba. The management’s own document shows 
that there was one Jitu Alahalo son of Bipan Muhato named 
in Form B Register and there was no question for the 
concerned workman to get his reinstatement by falsely re¬ 
presenting himself as litu Dhoba, In my opinion the said 
allegation that the concerned workman got reinstatement in 
nlaee of Jitu Dhoba is a complete myth and ds not at all 
supported by any evidence on record. 

On the consideration of the above facts it will be clear 
that the concerned workman was a workman of Mandal’s 
Kenduadih Colliery who was one of the concerned workman 
of Reference No. 22 of 1977 and had got reinsfalement and 
was subsequently stopped v/ork. 

The concerned wiorkman was slopped work without nsslcn- 
ing any reason. Admittedly no chargesheet was framed acainst 
him. It has not been establi-ihcd that the concerned workman 
had got reinstatement by inipcrsonatina some other person. 
Tt has been submitted on behalf of the concerned workman 
that his termination was nninstified ns his termination wi'h- 
out complying of Section 25r of the l.D. Act w'as quite 


illegal. The ca.se reported in 1984-Lab-I-C-1651 has been re¬ 
lied upon on behalf of tho concerned workman. Section 
2(oo) definies retrenchment whi.h means the termination by 
the employer of the services ot a workman ior any reason 
whatsoever otherwise than a puni.shment inflicted, by way of 
dis iplinary action but does not includt voluntary reiircment, 
'etirement on supcranmialisvi and termination on the ground 
of continued ill health. In the above decision it has been l eld 
that whe-ther the termination of service is brought about by 
voluntary or involuntary action, whether that result Is pro¬ 
duced by os'crlaet or by opefatloii of the provision of the 
Standing Orders the termination would be retrenchment with¬ 
in the meaning of Section 2(oo> of the l.D, Act .since the 
fact of termination is only relevant, howsoever produced 
Is irrelevant for applicability of Section 25F. It was further 
held that onue the tcrminuiion does not fall in one of the 
c.vccpted categories enumerated' in Section 2{oo), the termi¬ 
nation of service even it be accoiding lo automatic discharge 
from service under an agreement or by default of the work¬ 
men it would be rclrenchmcnt attracting, the compliance of 
Section 25F of the l.D. Act, Admittedly, th.e provision of 
■Section 25F was not complied in terminating the services 
of the concerned workman and on this score alone termi¬ 
nation of the services of the concerned workman cannot be 
sustained. I have already discussed above that in snb.stancc 
the concerned workman had given address correcTly as he 
was residing in village Tursabad with his brother-in-law. It 
has not been established that the concerned workman had 
impersonated any other person in eeffing bis reinstatement. 
As such the concerned workman cannot be dismissed from 
service on n mere technical grouiu! that he had not given 
the correct village address at the time of his appointment 
or when he had filed f) certificate for being reinstated in the 
job. The concerned workman had given his address of village 
Tursabad for being reinstated as his original address was 
noted ns Tursabad at the time of his appointment by the 
TStwhile management. In mv opinion the concerned w'oik- 
man cannot be held to have committed any miscondiiel. 

In view of the facts, evidence and circumslunces of the 
case discussed above 1 hold that the action of tlee management 

of Lohapatti Colliery of M/s. Bbarai Coking Coal J.td. in 
•erminating the services of ilte concerned workman is' not 
iiistified. The concerned workman is therefore reinstated 
from the date of his termination from service with all con¬ 
sequential benefits. 

This is ray Award.

Dispute referred to by the Central Ciovernment for adjudi¬

fication No. L-24012(1)/8LD.1V fflj dated 24-7-L581 of tnc 
Ministry of Labour run* thus : 

"Whether the refusal by iJie management of South 
Btdanda Colliery of Central coalfields Limited, 
P.O. flalanda, Uislt. Dhenkanal, Orissa, to recoru 
20-1-1929 in the Setviee Sheets of Shri A. P. Jena, 
Driver as the date of his birth, is justified'? If not, 
to what relief is the workman concerned entitled?” 

2. It is not in dispute and is admitted by both the panics 
that the second-party workman was the driver of the first- 
party management till 21-2-1981 when he was superannuated 
on his attaining the 60 yeais of age, his date of birth being 
21-2-1920, as noted in his Service Book. It i.s also admitted 
that the second-party workman challenged the entry in bis 
service book with regard tp his dale of birth us incorrect for 
the first lime dn 5-1-1980 asserting that his date of birth is 
20-1-1929 a ,<3 per entry in the School .Admission Register of 
flaladiabandha U.P. School and not 21-2-1921 as noted in 
bis Service Book. It is fmthcr admitted that the first-party 
management having refused to act on the basis of the certi¬ 
ficate produced by the second-party workman, there was a 
conciliation proceeding started at the instance of the second- 
party, and the conciliation having failed, the present reference 
has come up for adjudication. 

3. The substantial question that arises for cor;sidcraiic)n 
in this case is whether the date of birth of the second-party 
workman ns noted*in (he School Admission Register i.s or is 
not acceptable. 

4. Three witnes.sCs were examind for the second-partv 
workman and none for ihe first-parly management, Witness 
No, 3 for the sccond-partv'workmao is the workman himself. 
He asserts that he was reading in Baladiabandha L.P. School 
and that his date of birth as noted in the admission register 
of the said School Is 20-1-J929, Witness No. 2 for the second- 
party is the tlcadmastcr of Baladiabandha U.P. .School. He 
has produced the admission register, E,\t. 1, of Baladiabandha 
P.P. School and theirin mention is made against the name 
of the second-party that his dale (if birth wa? 2I)-1-I929. On 
a persual of Ext, 1 it appears that it is not a bound hooR as 
it consists of some IcKise papers being stitched in the middle. 
The cover page is also not there and consequeof/y it is very 
diflficult to know to which school it relates and to which year. 
There is also no page-mark or seal or any signature of any 
.luthoritv vouchsafing the correctness of the entries made in 
the register. The headmaster of the school who ntnde the 
disputed entry in the register is admittedly alive, but he js 


not c.vammcd to prove the said entry on the pretext of hia 
old age. Had the second-party approached the h 9 adma«ior to 
come as a witness to prove the entry in question and had b* 
demed on the ground of his old age, iiie matter vvould have 
been different, But 1 find from the cviden.c of the se-ond- 
party himself that no such approach was -ever made by him 
to the headmaster to come' ana depose lliai the disputed entry 
was made by him. Further 1 find tiom hie statement that 
when he approached the lieiidmaiiter in 1979 for a certificate, 
Ihc headmaster refused to comply viiih his request. No head¬ 
master would be have in such a lashton if an approach is made 
by any body, for the issue of certificate in his favour. The 
fact that the headmaster refused to issue any cettiricato when 
approached by the second-party for the said purpose clearly 
establishes that there is somoihing wrong in it and that is 
why the headmaster refused to comply with the request of 
Ihc second-party in the matter of issuance of school certi¬ 
ficate in his favour. To add to it, Baladiabandha U.P. School 
was upgraded in 1942 as would be evident from the statement 
of witness No. 2 for the second-party. If that be so, it is not 
understood how the name of the-second-party appeared in 
the admission register of Baladiabandha U.P. School if llic 
sccoiiu-paiiy loox Jns admission m the italadiauandtia L.E, 
School in 1934 as stated by him. This a. another circitinstance 
wmcti niilitalcs against the case of Ific second-party. Further 1 
find irom the senool admission register that not only the ag« 
ol tnc secOnd-party but also the age of some Others who loojc 
adnussion on the same day ol aamissiori or the se-ond-party 
is noted a.s 20-1-1929 and for all of them a sinfilo'man hai 
.signed the register as, their guardian. There are oJscv blanks 
here and there besides overwritings. In view of all these, and 
taking into consideration Ihc fact that at the time of entry into 
service no such copy of the school admissiofi rcgisicr was 
produced by the second-party in proof of his age, 1 am ot 
the view that the school admission register is created subse¬ 
quently to suit the purpose, This view of mine finds support 
Irom one more circum.staoce and that is that the .second-party 
having failed to produce any documentary evidence in support 
of his age, his medical examina’.ion was done and his date of

naiiou, he asserted his age to be 34 years but by appearance

concerned from time to time bid no effect. Had there been 
any corresppndcncc in this regard there would have been

said. But no .such correspondence ig forlhcoming on the 
ground that the request was made orally. Therefore, witness 
No. 1 for the workman cannot be believed on the point 
deposed to by him. Non-action of the second-party for a 
pretty long time is also a circumstance which goej against

j'ustificd.
